newsitem.title: USA: Storage space short after record Kansas wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Storage space short after record Kansas wheat crop.

text.p: A record Kansas wheat crop this year looks set to lead to a shortage of storage space, with concern growing about how farmers are going to handle this year's row crop harvest in the fall, grain dealers said.
"They are going to put milo (sorghum) on the ground in a lot of places, corn will probably go on the ground in some places. There is no room in the bins," a Kansas-based grain dealer said.
The Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service this week put the state's wheat crop at a record 492 million bushels.
The total was almost double last year's 255 million.

"There is a lot of stuff looking for a home and space is getting kind of tight around terminal markets so I don't think everyone is going to get the opportunity to move everything they want to," another Kansas dealer said.
Dealers said most farmers were looking to store wheat at grain elevators but were not yet prepared to sell it to them.
"All of it (the wheat) wants to move for storage. Selling (by farmers) is quiet," one Kansas dealer said.
Dealers noted some elevators were already only prepared to accept wheat if farmers committed to selling it to them.

"Some elevators aren't even going to handle as many commodities as they used to. They might just handle milo and beans and not corn or maybe corn and milo and not beans. There is just not the space out there," another dealer said.
Dealers also said the record crop had led to some tightness in the availability of railcars and trucks.
"Trucks' rates have come down a bit but are still at a premium to what they were a year ago and you can't buy a railroad car to save your soul," one dealer said
"The harvest has been very good (in Kansas) and we've had a lot of business there. The railcar situation is tight but certainly no crisis situation," said Union Pacific Corp spokesman John Bromley.
Sorghum, corn and soybeans are among the crops harvested in Kansas during the fall.
The Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service earlier this week forecast this year's corn crop at 351 million bushels, second only to last year's record high of 357.2 million.

The Kansas soybean crop was also seen the second highest on record at 73.6 million bushels, only slightly below last year's 74.0 million. Sorghum output was, however, seen dipping to 248.5 million bushels from last year's 354.2 million.
